correctness.rationale: The conditional two-binomial composition mixture is copied explicitly from the motivating source. The binomial-tail derivative telescopes to \(n inom{n-1}{m-1}z^{m-1}(1-z)^{n-m}\). After \(t=h/(1-h)\), the derivative sign is that of \(L(t)=a\log(1+t/p)-b\log(1+t/(1-p))\), with numerator \(a-(n-1)p+(a-b)t\) in its derivative. This implies at most one positive zero and yields every claimed boundary regime. The special four-person polynomial, exact optimizer \(8/13\), and endpoint/interior fractions were checked in exact rational arithmetic. The smooth-response persistence follows from finite polynomial coefficient convergence and nonzero second derivative at the strict optimizer. Direct package replay gave 23,097 exact rational checks; the infinite theorem rests on the analytic proof, not the checker.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Large-group Chernoff asymptotics do not determine the exact finite-group location or number of extrema. General hypergraph-affinity impossibility conditions constrain attainable type-frequency patterns but do not yield the one-parameter response profile. A more general binomial-tail variation theorem could subsume the statement, and that remains the residual priority risk, rather than demonstrated coverage.

value.rationale: Homophily and conformity jointly determine how many groups adopt protective behavior before any epidemic dynamics occur. The result gives a necessary-and-sufficient phase boundary for every group size and behavioral threshold, proves that adoption can reverse exactly once, identifies the smallest possible reversing group (four people), and computes a strict exact optimum that lies below both endpoint rates. The resulting benchmark separates behavioral aggregation from downstream epidemic threshold effects and has an explicit finite-steepness persistence consequence. It is not merely a numerical example, an arbitrary isolated parameter choice, or an epidemic claim unsupported by the model.
